expectations.text: waybar style.css sets window#waybar background to transparent (not a solid color)
waybar style.css uses border-radius on module containers (modules-left/center/right or individual modules)
expectations.evidence: style.css uses border-radius extensively: window#waybar > box has border-radius: 20px, #workspaces has border-radius: 14px, #clock has border-radius: 14px, and all right-side modules (#tray, #pulseaudio, #network, #cpu, #memory, #battery) have border-radius: 14px

expectations.text: waybar style.css uses @define-color to define a color palette (at least 5 named colors)
expectations.evidence: The style.css does NOT use @define-color at all. Colors are defined as inline hex values (e.g., #1e1e2e, #cba6f7, #cdd6f4). The Catppuccin Mocha palette is listed only in CSS comments, not as @define-color declarations.

expectations.text: waybar config.jsonc uses Nerd Font icons (unicode glyphs) in module formats, not plain text labels
expectations.evidence: config.jsonc uses Nerd Font unicode glyphs throughout: clock format uses '' (nf-md-clock), cpu uses '' (nf-md-cpu), memory uses 'b' (nf-md-memory), network-wifi uses '' (nf-fa-wifi), pulseaudio uses volume icons ['', '', ''], battery uses ['', '', '', '', ''], and custom/power uses '⏻' (power symbol)

expectations.text: waybar config.jsonc includes margin-top or margin properties to create the floating effect

expectations.evidence: config.jsonc modules-left contains "hyprland/workspaces" and the workspaces config block is keyed as "hyprland/workspaces"

expectations.text: waybar style.css uses button.active for workspace styling (not button.focused)
expectations.evidence: style.css contains: #workspaces button.active { color: #1e1e2e; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #cba6f7, #89b4fa); ... }. No button.focused selector is present.

expectations.text: waybar style.css includes state-based styling for at least 2 of: battery.warning, battery.critical, network.disconnected, pulseaudio.muted
expectations.evidence: All four states are styled: #battery.warning (color: #fab387), #battery.critical (color: #f38ba8 with blink animation), #network.disconnected (color: #f38ba8), #pulseaudio.muted (color: #6c7086)

expectations.text: waybar config includes at least 6 modules (workspaces, window, clock, pulseaudio/wireplumber, network, tray)
expectations.evidence: Config includes 10 modules: hyprland/workspaces, hyprland/window, clock, pulseaudio, network, tray, cpu, memory, battery, custom/power. All 6 required modules are present.

claims.evidence: Hex values in the CSS match the Catppuccin Mocha palette (e.g., #1e1e2e for Base, #cdd6f4 for Text, #cba6f7 for Mauve, #f38ba8 for Red)
Modules use border-radius: 14px with individual background colors creating distinct pill shapes, and the overall bar uses border-radius: 20px
margin-top: 8, margin-left: 10, margin-right: 10 combined with transparent window background and rounded box with semi-transparent background creates a floating appearance

suggestions.assertion: waybar style.css uses @define-color to define a color palette (at least 5 named colors)
suggestions.reason: This is a good discriminating assertion. Using @define-color is a best practice for maintainability in GTK CSS, and the output failed it by hardcoding hex values everywhere. However, note that many popular waybar themes in the wild do NOT use @define-color, so this tests a quality practice rather than correctness.
No assertion checks whether the config.jsonc is valid JSON with comments (JSONC). A malformed config would fail to load. Consider adding a structural validity check.

No assertion checks that the style.css and config.jsonc are internally consistent -- e.g., that every module referenced in the config has corresponding CSS styling. The output does this well but it goes untested.

eval_feedback.overall: Solid assertion set. The @define-color check is a useful discriminator that caught a genuine quality gap. Consider adding a structural validity assertion.
